Direct Harbor recovery trial

Bounded experimental trial. Production evaluation and Pages remain unchanged.

Download machine-readable results · Frozen input manifests · Workflow evidence excerpts

Decision

A specific blocker remains: recover valid submitted-artifact evidence before another comparison. The launch defect is corrected and credential-free provider checks passed. Both authorized live sessions completed, but neither produced a valid independent task grade. Stop scheduling; no adoption or skill-effectiveness conclusion is supported.

Codex 0.155.1 rejects reserved model_providers.openai before authentication; the supported trial_openai alias fixes startup. Stock Harbor/Codex reached real inference in both arms. Current and absent deployments matched except the three target-skill files. Both verifiers returned invalid/artifact, not measured incorrect answers. Four recovery slots are consumed; historical and cumulative charges remain unknown.

Credential-free launch repair

Codex 0.155.1 rejects the reserved configured provider ID openai during config loading, before authentication/model inference. All preceding stock-launch setup commands succeed. This reproduces the retained historical configuration defect; the original failed-run stderr itself was unavailable.

The second used the available compressed index route with by-hash disabled; signed metadata and package/hash pins remain unchanged. No dependency upgrade or oracle requalification was performed.

The user later explicitly authorized paid testing with unknown cost. The next pair remains bounded to the two remaining recovery slots; historical spend remains unknown.

Campaign usage

Four credentialed reservations consumed 4/4 recovery slots and 4/36 campaign slots: two historical failed launches plus the authorized current/absent pair. Two actual model sessions are now confirmed. Current reported 47,987 input (35,617 cached; 12,329 cache-write) and 637 output tokens; absent 47,842 input (35,525 cached; 12,276 cache-write) and 730 output. Cache counts are components, not additional input totals. Harbor native pricing estimates are $0.11417975 and $0.11659250 ($0.23077225 subtotal), not provider bills. Conservative estimates including all cached input at $20/M and output at $30/M are $0.97885 and $0.97874 ($1.95759 subtotal). Cumulative observed/estimated campaign spending remains unknown because prior usage and attributable billing are unavailable. The $2.64 pair preflight estimate was not an observed charge. User explicitly accepted unknown costs for testing. The operational $20 budget is not a guaranteed cap; a $4 scheduling threshold retained $16 nominal reserve, but unknown prior charges and in-flight usage can overshoot it. Scheduling is now disabled. Two diagnostic Actions runs added no paid attempts; no judge, inference retry or skill revision was used.

Sandbox and deployment boundary

Explicit user authorization replaces only the evaluated Codex inner-sandbox requirement with the disposable hosted runner/container boundary. Stock Harbor run/exec methods are inherited without command rewriting. No implementing-agent sandbox or approval mechanism was disabled. Historical Bubblewrap/Landlock failures remain in sandbox.json and are not a current gate.

Actual containers passed UID/GID 1000, CapEff=0, NoNewPrivs=1, Seccomp=2, writable output, fresh-session/auth checks, protected-path absence and deployment hashes. Docker metadata confirms no privilege, no added agent capabilities, cap_drop=ALL, default seccomp (no unconfined override), 2 CPUs, 2 GiB RAM, 256 PIDs, no host PID/network mode and no host mounts. No Docker socket, grader source, reference implementation, mutants or unrelated credential names were available.

Harbor native allowlist restricts the agent to api.openai.com using its separate disposable controller; only that controller needs NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW. Both actual agent preflights reached the API root (HTTP 421) while GitHub, raw GitHub, Microsoft Learn and metadata IP connections failed. Both later authenticated model sessions completed. DNS and the allowed API remain residual channels; web search and remote MCP were disabled. This is not a formal network-isolation proof.

The inference key must be accessible to Codex and can be read by code in the same environment. Container isolation does not conceal it. No auth file, secret-bearing environment dump, raw agent log or submission is exported. Preflight checks and host metadata are practical evidence, not a formal container-security proof or interactive-workstation equivalence.

The separate offline verifier and protected executable checks are unchanged from successful controls. Both latest live outcomes are invalid/artifact and unmeasured despite Harbor reward_valid=true. result_extraction_succeeded describes metadata recovery only; execution_completed describes native completion only. Best-effort root cleanup failed under dropped capabilities, but entire agent containers were verified removed. No privilege was added.

Repair diagnostics use the same stock launcher, UID, ownership and pins with external networking disabled. Corrected live config selects trial_openai while preserving API endpoint/authentication, OpenAI headers, WebSocket capability, model, effort and matched arms. The same runtime config function serves current and absent.

History

Original run 41952213509 explicitly received a runner shutdown signal. Cause remains unknown; exit 143 alone does not identify a Harbor timeout/crash. No original native grade survived. Its prior report is preserved as history below; the prior recommendation is superseded and does not show that the existing stack is better. The prior recovery report at 29f7765 is retained under history, including its zero-spend record and now-superseded native-sandbox requirement. The known-good and weak native observations were not rerun or rescored. The repaired pair ran c5a430a; f61201a was earlier packaging, while failed run 41966399157 executed 11bf0db. User later authorized the remaining two smoke attempts with unknown costs. Their successful process completion does not supersede the invalid-artifact observations.

Maintenance and remaining evidence

The unchanged oracle controls prove a narrow grading distinction: both pass the reference; only the good suite detects 2/2 defects. Both live sessions completed, but invalid/artifact outcomes are excluded. A successful workflow or numeric zero reward cannot establish a valid comparison.

The root cause is reproduced with the retained historical config through the same pinned stock launcher: Codex rejects reserved model_providers.openai before authentication. The original run's stderr was not retained, so the recovered reproduction is the causal evidence. trial_openai preserves endpoint/authentication/model/effort; actual runtime probes verified one HTTP POST on 503 and one silent stream ending after 60.2 seconds. WebSocket probing/fallback remains outside that no-retry observation.

Nineteen focused tests pass locally; eighteen ran on the executed live head. The new custom_tool_call fixture failed before the collector correction and passes after it. These completed live rollouts were not republished or reprocessed; activation and total tool usage remain unknown. No production full-suite or repeated oracle qualification was run.

Custom maintenance remains fixed staging/projection/reporting, a small live runner, pinned installation/ownership subclass, native-log sanitizer/checkpoint handler, diagnostic-only refusal fixture and verifier, signed snapshot transport helper, and a branch-only workflow. Two private Harbor methods remain overridden for home ownership and config upload. No upstream patch, added private hook or new execution layer was introduced. Provider defaults, native log/event schemas, task checksum deprecation and pinned egress sidecar still require compatibility review.

The compressed signed snapshot index selection fixed transport without changing package/image pins or signature/hash validation. The disposable external boundary remained unprivileged with dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, default seccomp, bounded CPU/RAM/PIDs, no host resources, API-only egress and separate offline verification. Root best-effort secret deletion can fail under these capabilities; verified container disposal is the actual cleanup boundary.

Existing task requirements, references, seeded defects, grader, PowerShell runner, runtime installer and target skill are unchanged. Valid output handoff, activation, natural skill selection, skill benefit, revision improvement and lower maintenance have not been established by this pair. Another skill still requires representative tasks, executable graders and controls.

Production components removed: none. APM, static checks, production evaluation, recurring workflows and Pages are untouched. Adoption is not justified by launch success alone.

Smallest next step: diagnose the submitted-artifact boundary with credential-free checks and bounded artifact-status metadata before authorizing any further model attempt. Retain native artifact-manifest status and non-content tool/completion classifications to distinguish no output, output rejection and transport failure. Do not repeat the full qualification campaign or expand the architecture. All recovery attempts are consumed.
